basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 31.' and it opens 'Vers. 31. Pater noster senex est. Putabant filiae Lot omne genus hominum ubique'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 31. Pater noster senex est. Putabant filiae Lot omne genus hominum ubique defecisse, nullumque virorum remansisse nisi patrem suum. Ideo hoc cogitaverunt ut ex patre semen servarent. Quarum adulterium Origenes multipliciter excusat, quia hoc non libidinoso animo sed studio reparandae prolis egerunt. Lot vero inexcusabilis est primo, quod angelo non credidit, deinde, quod vino inebriatus est; sicque minus peccatum fuit ei causa majoris criminis.
